summary: MWIR XBn-InAsSb barrier (HOT) cooled FPA, 1920×1536 at 10 µm pitch, operating at 150 K. No dedicated product datasheet was found; values come mainly from SCD's technical paper on its 10 µm InSb/XBn family, and some are taken from sibling devices (1280 XBn, 640 XBn).

notes.note: [B] Gershon et al. (SCD): 10 µm XBn arrays made in 1920×1536.

[B] ROIC table: full frame at 120 Hz with 4 video ports (60 Hz with 2 ports, 30 Hz with 1). The InSb datasheet [A] says ≥120 Hz, but its features list says ≥90 Hz. 2×2 binning supports up to 450 Hz [B].
[B]: 2.0 Me⁻ mode, the mode used for the XBn NETD measurement. Other ROIC modes are 0.3, 0.5 and 4.0 Me⁻.
[B]: 330 e⁻ in the 2.0 Me⁻ mode (260 e⁻ in ITR mode), measured at 77 K. At 150 K the noise may increase by up to 30%, i.e. up to about 430 e⁻ (derived).
[B]: typical 0.2 pA per pixel at 150 K, measured on the 1280×1024 XBn FPA with the same 10 µm pixel, not on the 1920.
Derived: 2.0e6 e⁻ / 2^13 for a 13-bit ADC [B], giving about 244 e⁻.
[C] SCD MWIR web page / Blackbird 1280 family datasheet search snippets: XBn band 3.6–4.2 µm, filter-defined. 1–4.2 µm available on request.

No value for the 1920 XBn. [B] gives 36 mK average (std 4 mK) for the Blackbird-640 XBn at F/3, 150 K, 50% well fill, 2.0 Me⁻ mode; no scene temperature stated. The InSb 1920 is <28 mK at 70% well fill, 2.5 Me⁻ [A].
Not stated for the XBn 1920. The InSb 1920 standard is f/3 (f/2 and f/4 optional). The XBn Mini Blackbird 1280 offers F/3.4 and F/4.
Not stated; no fill factor is given.
Not applicable: photon detector, not a microbolometer.
Approximation by the note-taker, based on the typical XBn QE of 70% [B] and the 3.6–4.2 µm band. Not a published curve.

The XBn pixel MTF is 0.36 at half Nyquist [B]. A 2017 SCD journal paper calls the device 'HOT Blackbird' and says it has been developed. SCD's current Blackbird 1920 datasheet covers only the InSb version (80 K, 1–5.4 µm).

sources: [B] Gershon et al. (SCD), 10 µm pitch family of InSb and XBn detectors for MWIR imaging: https://scdusa-ir.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/10um-pitch-family-of-InSb-and-XBn-detectors-for-MWIR-imaging.pdf
[C] SCD MWIR web page and Blackbird 1280 family datasheet (search snippets only)

SCD, Development and production of array barrier detectors at SCD, JEM 2017: https://scdusa-ir.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/DEVELOPMENT-AND-PRODUCTION-OF-ARRAY-BARRIER-DETECTORS-AT-SCD_published-in-JEM-2017.pdf
